content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"The final decision's path from evidence to conclusion is only partly traceable: the finding of 'no evidence of discriminatory animus' and the 'rebalancing of workload' rationale rest mainly on S2's statements, with no workload documents cited, and the record omits S1's account, C1's comparator information, and any analysis of the May 3 comment linking GLIFAA membership to the assignment."},"rc2":{"status":"pass","note":"Most characterizations are attributed to an identified source (Complainant, S2, C2), and the record explicitly notes S1 and C1 were not interviewed and no demographic data on C1 exists."},"rc3":{"status":"pass","note":"Events are dated and sequenced from the April 2018 interview through the May 2018 exchanges, the June 21, 2018 reassignment, and the August 14, 2018 complaint filing, though the date of the final decision and the review period for the hostile environment claim are not stated."},"rc4":{"status":"review","note":"The decision-maker is not named and the framework applied is shown (prima facie, legitimate reason, pretext, severe or pervasive), but the record does not show who authored the decision or whether Complainant's responses were considered, and S2's reasons for reassigning the portfolio are not documented in any contemporaneous record."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"The record does not stand on its own because S1, the key actor, was never interviewed, there is no comparator data for C1, no workload documentation supports the rebalancing explanation, and the C2 account conflicts with Complainant's on the May 8 incident, so an independent reviewer could not assess whether the conclusion is supported."}}}
